Answer: A
Reason: The chest X-ray (Figure 1b) demonstrates bilateral widening of the lower posterior mediastinum with smooth, lateral displacement of both paraspinal lines (indicated by arrowheads) and no evidence of vertebral destruction. This radiographic appearance is characteristic of diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (or similar lymphoproliferative disorders) presenting as bilateral paravertebral masses, whereas neurogenic tumors are typically unilateral and extramedullary hematopoiesis is usually associated with severe anemia and rib changes not described here.
